description:
FILED s530 (Fable), from a merge probe of s527d; PRE-EXISTING on main 0fb05a79 and identical on s527d's tree.

Reproducer (two lines in one file):
  my @b = sort </tmp/claude-1000/x-1/y/*.pl>; print scalar(@b),"\n";
  my @c = sort </tmp/claude-1000/x1/*.pl>; print scalar(@c),"\n";
perl: 1 / 0.  PCL: dies at load with `invalid number of arguments: 5` in
  (P-. "/tmp/claude-1000/x-1/y/*.pl>; print scalar(" #() ...)
-- the `<` after `sort` was lexed as less-than and everything up to the NEXT line's `>` became a string operand.
Controls (all agree with perl): `sort </etc/host*>`, `sort <*.pl>`, `<ABS/x-1/*.pl>` without sort, `reverse </etc/host*>`.
The trigger looks like the `-1` (a NUMBER after `-` inside the would-be glob: the term-end rule? a `-N` repair?).
Bisect which layer decides first: PPI on the vendored lib (dump the tokens) vs PCL's `_fix_ppi_glob_after_block`
and the `<...>`-after-a-list-operator repair s527d kept (the `*>` arm).
Where it belongs: Â§14 territory (`<...>` after a block / a list operator).  If PPI mis-lexes, it is a token row
for the next PPI batch (catalogue + report + registry first); if PPI is right and PCL's repair splits it, a PCL fix.
Also: the failure is a Lisp backtrace, not a tidy one-line error (the USER's rule: errors fail where perl's do, and are tidy).


=== DONE (s527g) ===
PPI mis-lexed it: §14's list-operator half (not a new §58 -- §14 already catalogues `<FH>` after a list operator; catalogue §14d).  PPI group AH, second pair (30d7356c TODO + 5c74a167 fix): `<...>` where perl expects a term -- after an operator and after a BUILTIN that takes an operand -- is ONE QuoteLike::Readline (toke.c yyl_leftpointy); the term test Operator.pm used for `~~` moved to PPI::Tokenizer::_term_expected and is shared (+ CORE::).  Un-TODOs the five §14 rows + a new `sort </tmp/x-1/y/*.pl>` row.  After a USER sub PPI cannot know (a declaration makes the list operator): PCL's Pl::Parser2::_repair_glob_pattern_cascade now also reads a y/ (s/ tr/ m/) derail (it required the Regexp to start with /).  Guards Pl/t/ppi-token-rows-01.t (builtin, return/reverse, user sub; inverse-verified on main), canary flip in Pl/t/misc-fixes-02.t (+ a user-sub canary).  The `*>` arm of _fix_ppi_glob_after_block STAYS (user subs: `foo <op/*>` still arrives as `< op / *>`).
subject: LOUD (Lisp backtrace): `sort </ABS/x-1/*.pl>` -- a glob after `sort` whose path holds `-DIGIT` is read as less-than; the source up to the NEXT `>` becomes one string operand
